Funny! Readers Digest is not the way it used to be. The pages are thinner. You can feel it. It is just not the same at all. It is still a good little book with stories, etc. but just not the way it used to be.

Architectural Digest in former years was a stodgy, slightly dull journal with archival records of worldwide interior design, on high quality paper. People would keep the issues for years considering it an historical record of design as sponsored by the affluent.

No more. In 2016 it was taken over by Amy Astley, the former editor of TEEN VOGUE. You read that right, Teen Vogue, and AD now is just as trendy and advertiser focussed, reimagined for the Instagram generation. Largely dedicated now to homes of celebrities or should we say, 'influencers.' To anyone who loves serious design as one of the useful arts, offensive, but I'm sure it has brought more corporate revenues. Because now AD has been able to sell the celebrity - besotted readers to the advertisers.

Amy has done this by changing the business model from subscription based to ad based. This means the readers are no longer the customers, but rather the product - to be handed over to the new customers, the advertisers. Predictably, AD content has been dumbed down to the clickbait level to bulk up readership with unsophisticated topics such as Kim Kardashian's new bathroom or, for variety, Kanye West's new bathroom.

Also, excessively focussed on New York City as if we all lived there. And much attention to a small circle of decorators who belong to the so-called AD100 - a group of business collaborators who made deals with the magazine. Not a serious journal at all any more, and not focussed on design at all.

People no longer save the issues. And by the way, there is no need to subscribe. Give them your email address and you will get TWO emails every day, so eager they are to tell readers what Instagram celebs are doing to their bathrooms.

If you are a new collector, you are better off digging for used and other deals. If you don't know a lot of classic, then this may be a way to gain some exposure but the value is not very good as many items are cheaper by a couple dollars if purchased direct from amazon.

For those with medium to large collections already you will probably return 80-90% of what they send you. I have only kept 2 or 3 of the 10 or so they have sent and had ~250 records. Returns roughly were based on 1/3 not being something I wanted, 1/3 being something I already had, 1/3 being overpriced.

Will probably cancel in another month or two but was holding out for Amazon to make some improvements based on previous comments. Primarily, they need to have set date each month to review what they are going to send and have a deadline to skip. Currently it is random and you have to login to amazon and view orders and there is ~24 hours or so that you may be able to catch it and skip. Way too random. Seems strategic of amazon to ship things banking on people not returning them if they have in hand. This seems shady and ultimately is some plan for Amazon to clear out inventory that isn't selling.

Another change Amazon still hasn't added despite suggestions, is a swap option. If each month there was an opportunity to swap for a few other choices, maybe I wouldn't be sending so many back. This could possibly still help them clear out inventory as greater chance of something I could actually want.

Given the value is poor many months, it is hard to recommend this for any collector. If you are disciplined about returns and have a convenient way to return amazon orders, then you have nothing to loose and maybe the continued loss in shipping expenses will motivate Amazon to implement changes. Maybe not as Amazon could just pass along the increased cost to consumers and continue poor ethics in how they handle employees.

Pros:
1. Really cute themes every month
2. Good variety of toys (nylon, rubber, etc) and you can customize how much of each kind you get by
contacting customer service. You can also customize to have a "toys only" box if you aren't interested in
treats
3. Great customer service in general
4. Good price for the number and quality of toys

Cons:
1. Hard nylon toys should ONLY be given to puppies - that way if they crack a tooth it isn't a permanent one.
As a general rule of thumb, if you can't make at least a small indent with your fingernail, it is too hard for
adult teeth. They really shouldn't be encouraging people to give rock-hard nylon toys to adult dogs.
2. If you have a dog that is over 75 lbs then this is not the box for you. The toys in the "large" size box were
on the small side for my GSD and are a full-on choking hazard for my mastiff. They should have an option
for giant breeds or they should explicitly state that when they ask you for your dog's breed, that they
aren't actually using that to choose the toy size - every dog in the large size box gets the same toys
regardless of whether they are a 60 lb collie or a 200 pound mastiff. It's extremely misleading for them to
ask what breed you have and then send everyone the same size toys anyway.
3. Their rubber toys are not nearly as heavy duty as kong or bullymake rubber toys. For true super chewers I
would choose bullymake. I have both subscriptions and I find that while barkbox is okay for my GSD, the
toys they provide are entirely unsafe, and not nearly durable enough, for my mastiff.

Conclusion:
I will keep getting this box for a couple of months because it has a nice selection of toys for my GSD and my smaller mixed-breed. However, they really should be offering a size up from the large box - I would say the toys in the large box would be more accurately described as being for medium-sized dogs like collies, smaller labs, and spaniels. The attached picture is of the rubber toy they sent after approximately 10 minutes with my mastiff (who isn't even full grown yet). The tail was ripped off by my GSD about 20 minutes after I took this picture. The whole things was in the garbage after about 45 minutes when I caught my mastiff eating pieces of the rubber. However, I will say that my experience with customer service was great and they sent out a replacement toy immediately, so no complaints there.
